content: 1. Glecaprevir/pibrentasvir increases the plasma levels or effects of vemurafenib by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter and reducing its metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 2. Glecaprevir/pibrentasvir may elevate the plasma concentration of substrates of the Breast Cancer Resistance Protein (BCRP). Caution and monitoring are recommended. 3. Venetoclax increases the levels or effects of glecaprevir/pibrentasvir by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Similarly, glecaprevir/pibrentasvir increases venetoclax levels via the same mechanism. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 4. Verapamil elevates the levels or effects of glecaprevir/pibrentasvir by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Conversely, glecaprevir/pibrentasvir increases verapamil levels through the same pathway. Caution and monitoring are advised. 5. Glecaprevir/pibrentasvir increases vinblastine levels or effects by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. 6. Glecaprevir/pibrentasvir increases vincristine levels or effects via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) inhibition. Therapy modification and close monitoring are necessary. 7. Voriconazole increases glecaprevir/pibrentasvir levels or effects by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 8. Glecaprevir/pibrentasvir increases voxilaprevir levels or effects by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. 9. Acetazolamide increases glecaprevir/pibrentasvir levels or effects by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance is minor or unknown. 10. Anastrozole increases glecaprevir/pibrentasvir levels or effects by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance is minor or unknown. 11. Cyclophosphamide increases glecaprevir/pibrentasvir levels or effects by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance is minor or unknown. 12. Drospirenone increases glecaprevir/pibrentasvir levels or effects by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance is minor or unknown. 13. Larotrectinib increases glecaprevir/pibrentasvir levels or effects by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance is minor or unknown. 14. Ribociclib increases glecaprevir/pibrentasvir levels or effects by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance is minor or unknown. 15. Voclosporin, an OATP1B1 inhibitor, may increase the concentration of OATP1B1 substrates, including glecaprevir/pibrentasvir. Monitor for adverse reactions and adjust therapy as needed. 16. Abiraterone increases glecaprevir/pibrentasvir levels or effects by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Caution and monitoring are advised. 17. Afatinib increases glecaprevir/pibrentasvir levels or effects via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) inhibition, and vice versa. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. 18. Glecaprevir/pibrentasvir increases aliskiren levels or effects by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Therapy modification and close monitoring are necessary. 19. Glecaprevir/pibrentasvir increases alvimopan levels or effects via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) inhibition. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. 20. Glecaprevir/pibrentasvir increases ambrisentan levels or effects by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter and potentially through OATP1B1/1B3 inhibition. Therapy modification and close monitoring are necessary. 21. Amiodarone increases glecaprevir/pibrentasvir levels or effects via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) inhibition, and vice versa. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. 22. Glecaprevir/pibrentasvir increases amitriptyline levels or effects by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Therapy modification and close monitoring are necessary. 23. Amobarbital decreases glecaprevir/pibrentasvir levels or effects by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised due to potential therapeutic loss. 24. Carbamazepine, a strong CYP3A4 and P-glycoprotein inducer, significantly decreases glecaprevir/pibrentasvir levels or effects by increasing metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 25. Glecaprevir/pibrentasvir increases carfilzomib levels or effects by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 26. Carvedilol increases glecaprevir/pibrentasvir levels or effects via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) inhibition, and vice versa. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 27. Caspofungin increases glecaprevir/pibrentasvir levels or effects by reducing metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 28. Ceftobiprole, an OATP1B1/1B3 inhibitor, increases glecaprevir/pibrentasvir levels or effects. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 29. Cenobamate decreases glecaprevir/pibrentasvir levels or effects by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Adjust the dose of CYP3A4 substrates as needed and monitor closely. 30. Glecaprevir/pibrentasvir increases cetirizine levels or effects by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 31. Glecaprevir/pibrentasvir increases cimetidine levels or effects via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) inhibition. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 32. Glecaprevir/pibrentasvir increases ciprofloxacin levels or effects by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Caution and monitoring are advised. 33. Clarithromycin increases glecaprevir/pibrentasvir levels or effects by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 34. Clotrimazole increases glecaprevir/pibrentasvir levels or effects by reducing metabolism. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 35. Cobicistat increases glecaprevir/pibrentasvir levels or effects by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 36. Glecaprevir/pibrentasvir increases colchicine levels or effects via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) inhibition. Avoid or use an alternative drug, especially in patients with renal or hepatic impairment. 37. Conivaptan increases glecaprevir/pibrentasvir levels or effects by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 38. Crizotinib increases glecaprevir/pibrentasvir levels or effects via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) inhibition. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 39. Cyclosporine, a moderate CYP3A4 and P-glycoprotein inhibitor, increases glecaprevir/pibrentasvir levels or effects by reducing metabolism. Avoid coadministration if cyclosporine exceeds 100 mg/day. 40. Glecaprevir/pibrentasvir increases dabigatran levels or effects by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Caution and monitoring are advised. 41. Dabrafenib decreases glecaprevir/pibrentasvir levels or effects by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 42. Danazol increases glecaprevir/pibrentasvir levels or effects by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 43. Danicopan increases glecaprevir/pibrentasvir levels or effects via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) inhibition. Dose reduction of P-glycoprotein substrates may be necessary to avoid serious adverse reactions. 44. Darunavir increases glecaprevir/pibrentasvir levels or effects by reducing metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug.
